html:
Biskupin is a fortified wooden settlement on a lake island in western Poland, built around 740 BCE by people of the Lusatian culture and found by a schoolteacher in 1933.

Tree ring dating shows the timber was cut over a few years in the 700s BCE. Inside a wooden rampart and breakwater, some 100 houses of the same plan stood in rows along log streets, home to perhaps a thousand people. The lake's water and mud preserved the wood. It was abandoned after a few centuries as the lake rose. Excavation continued even under the German occupation, and parts were rebuilt as an open air museum with a yearly archaeology festival. Prewar Poland made it a symbol of a deep national past, long before the baptism of Poland and the state of the Polish kings.
sum: Biskupin is a fortified wooden settlement on a lake island in western Poland, built around 740 BCE by people of the Lusatian culture and found by a schoolteacher in 1933.
